Subject: RE: Tenancy discussion — recap + open questions

Hi Alice — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and the questions we promised to follow up on.

Summary of what we heard today:
- Primary workload: nightly EHR export parsing + on-demand clinician query assistant (latency-sensitive).
- Compliance: PHI in transit + retention policy requires 36 months of audit logs.
- Traffic profile: ~250 concurrent users at peak, spiky during morning rounds (10–12am local).

Primary tenancy concerns you raised:
1) Noisy neighbor risk — you want guarantees that a scheduled batch job from another tenant won't push your median latency above 300ms for interactive queries.
2) Isolation boundary — you prefer CPU/GPU reservation or dedicated tenancy for models handling PHI.
3) SLOs & fallback — ask for an automatic fallback path if the preferred dedicated pool is saturated.

Open technical items for us to answer (can Sean chime in):
- Expected 95th/99th percentile latency targets for the clinician assistant flow (your target numbers would help).
- Whether the batch EHR export must be on the same tenancy as the interactive inference.
- Acceptable data residency and audit log retention (we heard 36 months but want it on record).

Next steps we propose:
- Sean to provide a short tech note on how Redwood Dedicated separates NVidia GPU pools vs our shared-hosted isolation mitigations (kernel priority, soft reservation, KV cache pinning).
- We’ll sketch a fallback routing plan: primary -> dedicated pool; if saturated, route to quantized lower-cost variant in dedicated burst pool; final fallback to hosted with rate-limited concurrency and stronger throttling.
- I'll schedule a follow-up call two business days out to review the short tech note, plus a DRAFT SLA for PHI workloads (attached).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-topology.png (diagram), SLA-draft-v1.pdf (draft language).

Thanks — Vanessa

Hi Alice — quick technical notes below, wanted to put concrete options on the table.

1) Physical isolation (hard reservation): When customers want absolute separation we recommend Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) where compute is dedicated to the tenant. That provides isolated hosts and KMS/HSM control.

2) Dedicated capacity (soft physical reservation): Redwood Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools for customers; pools can be single-tenant at the rack level depending on contract. We can offer a contract option for dedicated appliance assignment (effectively physical capex-like reservation) — will require a procurement timeline.

3) Hosted with mitigations (shared infra): For faster time-to-value our Hosted API uses scheduling knobs: kernel isolation, priority queues, KV-cache pinning, per-tenant fairshare. This reduces noisy neighbor risk but doesn't guarantee physical isolation.

4) Fallback and audit metadata: Any fallback route preserves request-level metadata (tenant id, request id, model version). We persist audit logs to a customer-specific retention store and can configure the 36-month retention with export hooks to your S3.

5) Proposal for SLA behavior:
- Primary: Dedicated pool with burst capacity up to X GPUs (to be sized).
- Burst fallback: Quantized model variant within Dedicated burst pool (lower accuracy but faster throughput).
- Final fallback: Hosted API with rate-limited concurrency and transaction tagging; in fallback we will proactively notify both incident and billing channels.

Action items:
- Vanessa/Marissa: I’ll send a one-page topology + table mapping tradeoffs (attached).
- PulseMed: Confirm whether hard physical isolation is a deal-breaker or if a contractual committed dedicated pool suffices.

Sean
